definitions.explanation: A private house where rooms are rented, often with meals provided.
The act of staying at such accommodation.

examples.japanese: {学生|がくせい}の{時|とき}、{下宿|げしゅく}に{住|す}んでいた。
examples.english: When I was a student, I lived in a boarding house.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}の{近|ちか}くで{下宿|げしゅく}している。
{下宿|げしゅく}の{家賃|やちん}は{月|つき}五{万|まん}{円|えん}だ。
examples.english: The rent for the boarding house is 50,000 yen a month.

examples.japanese: {下宿|げしゅく}の{大家|おおや}さんが{親切|しんせつ}だ。
examples.english: The landlord of the boarding house is kind.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}と{同|おな}じ{下宿|げしゅく}に{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: I live in the same boarding house as my friend.

examples.japanese: {下宿|げしゅく}を{探|さが}している。
examples.english: I'm looking for a boarding house.

examples.japanese: {下宿|げしゅく}を{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}した。
examples.english: I moved out of the boarding house.

examples.japanese: この{街|まち}に{下宿|げしゅく}することにした。
examples.english: I decided to board in this town.

examples.japanese: {下宿|げしゅく}{生活|せいかつ}を{始|はじ}めた。
{下宿|げしゅく}には{食事|しょくじ}がつく。

notes:
{下宿|げしゅく} refers to a boarding house or the act of lodging, traditionally popular among students.

VERBAL USE:
{下宿|げしゅく}する: to board, to lodge

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {下宿|げしゅく}を{探|さが}す: to look for lodgings
- {下宿|げしゅく}に{住|す}む: to live in a boarding house
- {下宿|げしゅく}{代|だい}/{下宿|げしゅく}{料|りょう}: lodging fee
- {下宿|げしゅく}{先|さき}: place of lodging
- {下宿|げしゅく}{生活|せいかつ}: boarding house life

TRADITIONAL FEATURES:
Historically, {下宿|げしゅく} included meals ({食事|しょくじ}つき) and were run by a landlord/landlady ({大家|おおや}さん). Common for university students away from home.

MODERN CONTEXT:
Less common today as アパート (apartments) and マンション (condominiums) have become the standard for student housing.
